cluster_summary: This cluster contains authentication vulnerabilities where the code fails to correctly await asynchronous password validation, skips required authentication validation on login, suffers from race conditions on single-use token consumption due to non-atomic updates, or omits sanitization of authentication data after retrieval. These flaws can lead to authentication bypass, unauthorized access, or reuse of single-use tokens.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Use optimistic locking by including the original array contents in the WHERE clause of the update query, so that if another request has already modified the array, the update fails..

mechanism.typical_fix: Use optimistic locking by including the original array contents in the WHERE clause of the update query, so that if another request has already modified the array, the update fails.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use optimistic locking by including the original array contents in the WHERE clause of the update query, so that if another request has already modified the array, the update fails.
sub_patterns.name: Race condition on single-use token removal without atomic conditional update
sub_patterns.root_cause: Read-then-write sequence on an array of single-use tokens without atomic conditional update allows concurrent requests to both validate and remove the same token because the update does not verify the token's current presence.
